description:
Result handling inside the concurrent streams both distorts measurement and
is inconsistent between the two benchmarks.

1. FULL MATERIALIZATION UNDER THE GIL: every stream calls
   `cursor.fetchall()` for every query:
   - TPC-H: benchbox/core/tpch/throughput_test.py:238 `rows = cursor.fetchall()`
     then `result_count = len(rows)`.
   - TPC-DS: benchbox/core/tpcds/throughput_test.py:314-315 fetchall() then
     the result is DISCARDED.
   fetchall materializes the entire result set into Python objects while
   holding the GIL. For embedded engines (DuckDB) that release the GIL during
   query execution but not during Python-object materialization, this
   serializes result handling across streams -- an artificial bottleneck that
   grows with result size and stream count, again masking real platform
   scaling. It is also timed inside execution_time_seconds.

2. INCONSISTENT ROW-COUNT SEMANTICS: TPC-H reports len(rows); TPC-DS hardcodes
   result_count = 0 (throughput_test.py:365). Downstream the adapter maps this
   to `rows_returned` (execution.py:427, :... ), so TPC-DS throughput rows all
   report 0 rows -- rows/sec and any result-volume sanity check are impossible
   for TPC-DS, and the two benchmarks are not comparable.

Fix: (a) use a row-count that does not require full Python materialization
where the driver supports it (e.g. consume the cursor / use rowcount / fetch
in bounded batches), and only materialize when validation actually needs the
rows; (b) make TPC-DS report real row counts like TPC-H; (c) document the GIL
implication for embedded engines so users interpret in-process throughput
correctly.

preserves.behavior: Result-count validation used by PlatformAdapterConnection still fires when enabled.

prior_art.concept: benchbox/core/tpch/throughput_test.py:238 — the len(fetchall()) pattern to replace with a non-materializing count where possible.
benchbox/platforms/base/connection_wrappers.py:PlatformAdapterConnection — where result validation already inspects platform_result; the right layer to standardize row counting.

verifications.description: TPC-DS throughput rows report non-zero counts where results exist

work_units.notes:
Prefer cursor.rowcount or a bounded consume loop over fetchall(); fall
back to len(fetchall()) only where the driver gives no count and
validation needs rows anyway.

Done: count_query_rows() added to connection_wrappers.py; also fixed
PlatformAdapterCursor._extract_rows()'s first_row-over-rows_returned
priority bug (see completed_note) and made .rows lazy.
